chunks: Ali, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), said:

He was asked about a man whose wife had become pure from her menstruation, so he said, 'So-and-so woman is divorced,' and a group was listening to his speech, and he did not say to them, 'Bear witness.' Does the divorce occur upon her? He said: 'Yes, this is witnessing.'

key_terms.فُلَانَةُ: so-and-so woman (a placeholder name used in legal examples)

ai.seo_question: Does a divorce count if the husband says it in front of a group but doesn't tell them to witness it?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the concept of 'shahadah' (witnessing) is interpreted broadly to include any competent listeners who hear the divorce formula, rather than requiring formal appointment as witnesses. This reflects the Shia juristic view that the validity of talaq relies on the public declaration and the presence of witnesses who perceive it, even if they are not explicitly summoned to testify, thereby simplifying the procedural requirements for divorce.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Safwan Bin Yahya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man whose wife was pure from her menstruation, so he said, ‘So and so woman is divorced’, and a group was listening to his speech, and he did not say to them, ‘Bear witness’. Does the divorce occur upon her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, this is witnessing’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Safwan ibn Yahya who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

was asked about the case of a man whose wife becomes clean of Hayd (menses) and he says this: ‘So and so is ‘Taliq’ (let go, divorced) and a people hears his statement but he does not ask them to bear witness: if divorce takes place or not, he (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, is bearing witness.’”
